create.name: Austin Zen Center / Zenkeiji
create.bio:
Austin Zen Center, whose temple name is Zenkeiji, is a Soto Zen community in central Austin, Texas, teaching in the line of Shunryu Suzuki. It grew from a weekly sitting started in 1995 by two friends; a small dedicated zendo followed in 1998, dedicated by Seirin Barbara Kohn of San Francisco Zen Center, and the group incorporated as Austin Zen Center in 2000. Since 2001 it has occupied a former Quaker meeting house on Washington Square, just north of the University of Texas, and its temple name honours Zenkei Blanche Hartman, who sent Kohn to guide it. Kohn, Kosho McCall and Mako Voelkel led it in turn, and Rev. Choro Antonaccio has been guiding teacher since 2023.

The centre now spans three buildings with a zendo, residential space, classrooms and a library. Beginners can learn zazen most Saturday mornings and stay for the Saturday programme of sitting, chanting and a Dharma talk; weekly sittings, study and discussion groups are free, and there is an online zendo. Private meetings with the guiding teacher and practice leaders, a fall practice intensive and the week-long Rohatsu sesshin in December deepen the practice, and its recent talks are published as a podcast.

courses.title: Beginner's Zazen Instruction
courses.description: An hour of meditation instruction and temple orientation in the zendo, most Saturdays at 8 am and on the last Tuesday evening of each month, with time for questions. Saturday attendees can stay on for the morning programme of zazen, service and a talk.

courses.title: Rohatsu Sesshin
courses.description: A week of intensive sitting, walking, eating and working in silence that closes the centre's fall practice intensive and leads into its celebration of the Buddha's awakening. Participants commit to at least two days, and some prior retreat experience is advised.
courses.price: Member Registration $45 per day; Non-Member Registration $55 per day

courses.title: Practice Discussion and Dokusan
courses.description: Private meetings during the weekly zazen schedule: formal dokusan with the guiding teacher, Rev. Choro Antonaccio, or a less formal practice discussion with a lay entrusted teacher or the tanto, to talk over one's sitting and daily life.

free_resources.title: Austin Zen Center Dharma Talks
free_resources.description: A podcast library of Saturday Dharma talks recorded at the centre since January 2024 by its teachers and visitors, playable on the page or through the main podcast apps.

free_resources.title: Chants for Services
free_resources.description: The texts the sangha chants through the week, with downloadable versions, including the Heart Sutra in Sino-Japanese, Dogen's Fukanzazengi and Genjo Koan, a list of women ancestors and the robe chant.
